new_statements.quote: Формальное выделение существительного в редуцированных вариантах сибирского пиджина связано с появлением «квази-суффиксов». Для существительных сибирского пиджина характерно достаточно устойчивое ударение, которое обычно падает на предпоследний слог, и лишь в редких случаях – на последний слог слова (дровá) или на третий от конца (дóжика 'дождь').
new_statements.translation: The formal marking of the noun in the reduced variants of Siberian pidgin is connected with the appearance of 'quasi-suffixes'. Nouns of Siberian pidgin are characterised by fairly stable stress, which usually falls on the penultimate syllable, and only in rare cases on the last syllable of the word (drová 'firewood') or on the third from the end (dózhika 'rain').
new_statements.citation: Перехвальская, Е. В. 2008. Русские пиджины. Санкт-Петербург: Алетейя. (PDF = author's manuscript 'All_RusPid.doc', 248 pp; Part I, Chapter 3 'Очерки по грамматике русских пиджинов', section 'Части речи в редуцированном пиджине' > 'Имя существительное')
new_statements.locator: manuscript p. 96 (PDF page 96 of 248; printed-page number of the Aleteya edition not verified), end of the section 'Имя существительное'; verified against the rendered page image
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: (the PDF's metadata: 'Microsoft Word - All_RusPid.doc', 248 pp.) rendered at PDF page 96 (page render) — the page carries the printed folio '96' and its last paragraph reads exactly: 'Как мы видим, ни в руссенорске, ни в говорке существительное формально не выделено среди слов других грамматических классов. Это, однако, произошло в сибирском пиджине. Формальное выделение существительного в редуцированных вариантах сибирского пиджина связано с появлением «квази-суффиксов». Для существительных сибирского пид-жина характерно достаточно устойчивое ударение, которое обычно падает на предпоследний слог, и лишь в редких случаях – на последний слог слова (дровá) или на третий от конца…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in the (Far Eastern/Ussuri) Chinese Pidgin Russian noun is stable and normally on the penultimate syllable; a few nouns have final stress (drová) or antepenultimate stress (dózhika). Cherepanov 1853 (p. 373) says of the Kyakhta variety that words are pronounced syllable by syllable, losing stress/pitch prominence on any one syllable, or that stress is placed mostly on the middle syllable (mo-ló-ko, zha-ré-ko, du-rá-ki, ledenéza), which he treats as an effect of effort in pronouncing a hard word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: Rare final stress (дровá) and antepenultimate stress (дóжика 'rain') in nouns (2008, p. 96); adjectives that kept the -j ending have final stress: слепóй, молодóй, другóй, чужóй (2006 autoreferat p. 15; 2008 the scanned text); ходи 'go' stressed on the last syllable with a variant on the first (2008 ms. p. 127 and fn.); рубли 'rouble' stressed on the first syllable (2008 ms. p. 127); хочу 'want' stressed on the first syllable (Shprintsin 1968, p. 93). 2008 ms. p. 20: Chinese-origin lexemes reduced the Chinese tone system to two tones. APiCS ch. 65 §4: /ɯ/ is always stressed, [ə] is unstressed.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns nouns of the Siberian (Far Eastern/Ussuri) variety, based on the author's Dictionary of Siberian pidgin (193 nouns) compiled from 19th-20th-century written sources and late-20th-century recordings of Udihe/Nanai/Chinese ethnolects; word-level, citation forms. Chinese-speaker ethnolects are reported (Jabłońska 1957 via Shprintsin 1968 and Perekhvalskaya 2008) to replace stress by tone, a claim Shprintsin rejects.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog kjac1234 covers all varieties of Chinese Pidgin Russian: the Kyakhta/Maimachen trade pidgin (18th-19th c.), the Far Eastern / Ussuri variety that Perekhvalskaya calls 'сибирский пиджин (дальневосточный вариант)' (late 19th-20th c.), and the Harbin variety; APiCS ch. 65 treats them as 'basically one language which existed in several varieties'. The quoted statement (Perekhvalskaya 2008) is about the Far Eastern/Siberian variety and specifically about nouns; the older primary statement (Cherepanov 1853, p. 373) is about the Kyakhta variety and says stress is lost in syllable-by-syllable pronunciation or falls mostly on the middle syllable. No separate glottocodes exist for the varieties.

sources.note: No dedicated phonology chapter (TOC checked). Ms. p. 96 (noun section): nouns of Siberian pidgin have fairly stable stress usually on the penultimate syllable, rarely final (дровá) or antepenultimate (дóжика). Ms. p. 20: Chinese-lexicon tones reduced to two. Ms. p. 127: ходи final-stressed (variant initial), рубли initial-stressed; p. 96 area: adjectives in -j keep final stress. Ch. 2 reports Jabłońska 1957 as claiming Chinese speakers replace word stress by (3rd) tone.
